question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**staff**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Staff**" refers to a group of people who work for** an organization or business**.
 
• The word is commonly used to refer to employees who are not in management positions.
 
• In the context of the given question, "**staff**" is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

​Correct Passage:__ *Twenty five years ago, few people realised that computers were about to become part of our daily lives. This short period of time has seen enormous changes, in business, education and public administration. Jobs which took weeks to complete in the past are now carried out in minutes. People who spent all day copying and checking calculations are now freed from these boring tasks. Students have become as familiar with hardware and software as their parents were with pencils and exercise books.*

*Computerisation of public records has enabled government departments to analyse the needs of citizens in detail. Some of us may wonder, however, life has really improved as a result of these changes. Many jobs disappeared, for example, when intelligent machines took over the work. Employers complain that clerical **staff** have become dependent on calculators and cannot do simple arithmetic.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 **(**soldiers**) refers to members of a military force who are trained to fight in wars or battles.
 
• **Option 3** (**messengers**) refers to people who are tasked with delivering messages or information from one person or place to another.
 
• **Option 4** (**religions**) is not a grammatically correct option to fill in the blank as it is a plural noun and does not fit the sentence structure. However, it could be used in a different context to refer to different belief systems or faiths.
